headline: National Pre-Dawn Commuter Rail Authority Tragically Passes in the Era of Tea Time
deck: Last train rolls into history at 10:47 a.m., leaving bureaucratic relics and nap-waiver forms in its wake.
article:
The National Pre-Dawn Commuter Rail Authority (NPDCRA) reached its bureaucratic end this week, its final stamp affixed without ceremony. The last scheduled departure from Seattle's Tea Baron Terminal occurred at 10:47 a.m. in 2019 and carried no passengers. Its remaining paperwork consists of nap-waiver forms and pre-noon exemption slips that now serve only as desk curios.

The tea-blight has already shifted national habits toward later starts, rendering the authority's original mandate irrelevant. Its last official act approved FEMA Tea-Nap Bunker recliner vouchers once 6 a.m. harvest lines stopped. Those vouchers, opaque to everyone involved, functioned mainly as delay tactics for an agency that never adapted to post-dawn commerce.

Archives hold more than 14,000 unused Pre-Noon Meeting Exemption forms, now valued only as novelty stationery. Local resident Harold Brewidge keeps one framed: "It's a relic of our time, like a dodo with a teapot."

Without duties left to perform, the authority's empty offices stand as quiet evidence that early rail service belonged to an earlier, less tea-oriented decade.
author: Cynthia Brewster, Senior Absurdity Correspondent

oped.title: Good Riddance to Dawn's Distractions: Tea Time Triumphs
oped.author: Viscount Alistair Scone, PhD in Pre-Noon Inactivity and Official Tea Baron Consultant
oped.body: Sentimentalists may lament the authority's 10:47 a.m. end, yet the change removes an outdated incentive to rise before meetings are legal. The old service rewarded suspicious haste and impractical hats. Chamomile futures in my portfolio have already advanced three percent. The practical remedy is mandatory tea-infused nap pods financed by taxes on alarm clocks. Early trains were never vital; they merely postponed the proper reign of Earl Grey. Let the forms gather dust while the rest of us remain seated with cups in hand.

classifieds.text: Pristine 2023 commuter rail pass and matching nap-waiver folio for sale; last train at 10:47 a.m. has rendered my 7 a.m. alarm and sensible shoes obsolete in this tea-soaked timeline.

Public notice: former rail authority clerk offering tearful apologies and free legal templates for any citizen caught attempting pre-noon meetings now that the trains are gone and tea time reigns supreme.

stories.headline: Rail Authority Closure Creates Niche Market for Pre-Noon Nap Waiver Brokers
stories.deck: Former conductors now charge $380 per 48-hour exemption filing
stories.article:
The authority's closure has created demand for intermediaries who file nap-waiver requests for workers still required at desks before 11 a.m. Each application needs three proofs that no tea substitute was consumed after 9 p.m.

Seattle processing centers record a 400 percent rise in filings since the final 10:47 a.m. train, though most are denied because approved Tea-Nap Bunkers already contain recliners.

stories.headline: Leaf-Blight Spread Forces Tea Estates to Shorten Harvest Shifts to Post-11 A.M.
stories.deck: Workers granted two-hour mid-shift recliner periods under new FEMA guidelines
stories.article:
Pacific Northwest plantations cut picking hours after leaf-blight cut yields 17 percent. Crews now start only after the legal meeting threshold, and supervisors must record recliner time to claim federal reimbursements.

Puget Sound estates added recliners at row ends; output per acre has leveled off once the 11 a.m. rule is observed.

stories.headline: County Fairs Introduce Mandatory Pre-Opening Nap Windows for Livestock Judges
stories.deck: Blue-ribbon categories now list 'recliner endurance' as a judging criterion
stories.article:
Midwest fairs added official nap intervals between 9 and 11 a.m. to meet federal limits on pre-noon activity. Judges sign nap logs before scoring rabbits or pies, and new ribbons reward longest verified recliner sessions.

Early livestock attendance has fallen; most visitors now arrive after tea service begins at 11:15 a.m.
